impacts.claim: Train A changes core Linear intake, automation, workflow, quality, and release-governance modules.
impacts.evidence: DEC-009 and DVD-219 through DVD-225 explicitly define the combined Train A scope.
impacts.next_verification: Review the final diff and traceability matrix before UAT handoff.

impacts.claim: The executable tools add no third-party runtime dependency but the live runner depends on Linear GraphQL availability and schema compatibility.
impacts.evidence: Both tools import only Python standard-library modules; the Linear endpoint and error contract are documented by Linear.
impacts.next_verification: Run py_compile, offline tests, and one authorized live dry scan before human UAT.

impacts.claim: Live scans process issue descriptions/comments and require a Linear token, so config, reports, and receipts must preserve the secret and project-memory boundary.
impacts.evidence: The token is environment-only; runtime files are ignored; the ledger omits body and token values; write operations use allowlists and runtime authorization.
impacts.next_verification: Run focused ledger tests and staged/private safety scan; inspect generated runtime files locally only.

impacts.claim: The new tools affect startup, daily Linear operation, development readiness, PR review, UAT, and version cadence documentation.
impacts.evidence: Core rules now link AUTOMATION_RUNBOOK, CHANGE_IMPACT, and TRACEABILITY into START_HERE, AGENTS, WORKFLOW, QUALITY_GATE, and UAT_TEMPLATE.
impacts.next_verification: Run strict validator and complete the non-engineering Owner walkthrough in UAT.

impacts.claim: Automation safety and evidence-state claims require deterministic tests, not documentation-only assertions.
impacts.evidence: Focused tests cover routing, bilingual output, credentials, write gates, idempotency, partial failure, trace states, evidence paths, and impact blockers.
impacts.next_verification: Run the full source suite and the extracted candidate-package suite.

impacts.claim: Only a human can confirm that the report, setup, queue routing, write boundary, and traceability matrix are understandable and useful.
impacts.evidence: DEC-009 requires one consolidated Train A human UAT and release policy forbids Codex self-acceptance.
impacts.next_verification: Owner completes project-os/audit/UAT_v0.6.0.md and explicitly passes or fails.

impacts.claim: Train A ships as a versioned GitHub Release asset; rollback restores v0.5.0 while preserving runtime state and project-specific audit memory.
impacts.evidence: Version planning and release policy keep generated zip assets out of source and require human UAT before tag/release.
impacts.next_verification: Verify candidate zip, digest, extracted validation, Draft PR, and documented v0.5.0 rollback path.

test_plan: Run py_compile for both new tools.
Run all Python unit tests, including intake and traceability suites.
Run the deterministic offline fixture twice and compare outputs.
Run private staged safety gate and inspect public tracked advisory.
Build the v0.6.0 candidate zip, extract it, validate it, and run its tests.
uat_plan: Owner runs or reviews the fixture queues and bilingual summary.
Owner confirms the live dry-run credential/setup path is understandable.
Owner confirms scheduled scans cannot modify local product code.
Owner reviews the triple write gate and sanitized ledger boundary.
Owner uses the impact and traceability reports to explain what is ready, pending, and not yet released.
rollout: After explicit v0.6.0 UAT Pass, merge the Draft PR, tag the merge commit, publish the verified zip and digest, then close Linear issues/project.
rollback: Before release, discard the candidate branch. After release, reinstall the v0.5.0 package from its GitHub Release while preserving LOCAL_OVERRIDES, audit history, runtime config/ledger, and project-specific safety decisions.
